A COMPLEX question (Deliberate lane) so the episode opens with intent='question' (record.py would NOT record it). episode-upgrade-followup then continues the same topic with an ACTIONABLE request; ClassifyRequest returns intent='task', continues_prior=true; OpenEpisode attaches AND bumps the episode's intent question->task, so the episode now records. message.content: Walk me through how we'd re-architect the orders service write path to survive high write contention — the locking strategy (optimistic vs pessimistic and why), the schema changes it implies, the migration sequence, and the failure modes to watch. I want the full design reasoning, not code yet.

scripted_model_responses.content: Optimistic locking wins when conflicts are rare — no lock held, a version column, retry on conflict; it degrades under high contention because retries pile up. Pessimistic locking holds a row lock so writers serialize cleanly, at the cost of throughput and deadlock risk. For a high-contention orders table the usual answer is optimistic with a bounded retry plus queueing the hot rows.
